banner.text: Berkeley Unified School District is a separate government with its own elected school board. These numbers come from BUSD's budget, not the City's.

cites.quote: The Berkeley Unified School District Board of Education, also called the School Board, is comprised of five elected directors
Each year before June 30 the School Board is required by law to pass a balanced budget.

year.text: BUSD's year runs July 1 to June 30, like the City's [fiscal year](glossary:Fiscal Year (FY)), so its 2026-27 budget lines up with the City's {year}.

cites.quote: Local Educational Agencies (LEAs) are required to adopt a budget prior to July 1 of each year in order to authorize the expenditure of funds.
The projected ending fund balances for the Measures as of June 30, 2027
For the 2026-27 fiscal year, the Berkeley Unified School District's (BUSD) combined General Fund is projected to receive $248.2 million in revenue.

total.quote: For the 2026-27 fiscal year, the Berkeley Unified School District's (BUSD) combined General Fund is projected to receive $248.2 million in revenue.

amount.quote: The primary source of funding is State revenue from the Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF), contributing $122.9 million with $116.1 base funding and $6.8 million as supplemental funding.

about.text: The State's Local Control Funding Formula: $116.1 million of base funding, and $6.8 million of supplemental funding set by how many students are English learners, foster youth or eligible for free and reduced-price meals.

cites.quote: The primary source of funding is State revenue from the Local Control Funding Formula (LCFF), contributing $122.9 million with $116.1 base funding and $6.8 million as supplemental funding.

The District is projected to receive $6.8 million in Supplemental Funding, which is determined by the percentage of pupils eligible for free and reduced-price meals, English Language Learner students, and Foster Youth.

amount.quote: The second largest funding source comes from local parcel tax Measures, which provide a total of $68.8 million, or almost 30% of the total revenue.

about.text: Three taxes Berkeley voters approved for the schools. BUSD says they support small class sizes, enrichment programs, educator salaries, and facilities safety and maintenance. [Each tax, below](page:schools#parcel-taxes).

cites.quote: BUSD is grateful for this vital funding from Berkeley taxpayers, which supports small class sizes, enrichment programs, educator salaries, and facilities safety and maintenance.

about.text: A credit, not a cost: other district funds, such as Adult Education, the Cafeteria and Child Development, pay the General Fund for the support services it gives them.

cites.quote: Other Funds including the Adult Education, Cafeteria and Child Development Funds are projected to pay $0.6 million in indirect costs to the Unrestricted General Fund for support services.

paragraphs.text: BUSD plans to spend $249.5 million from its General Fund in 2026-27 and to take in $248.2 million.

paragraphs.text: In the part of its General Fund that isn't set aside for specific programs, BUSD projects deficit spending, spending more than it takes in, of $2.3 million in 2026-27, $0.4 million in 2027-28 and $0.2 million in 2028-29.

cites.quote: The Multi-Year projections for the Unrestricted General Fund reflect the following balances for each year. 2026-27 2027-28 2028-29 Deficit Spending $2.3 million $0.4 Million $.2 million

paragraphs.text: BUSD says it has met the State's required 3% reserve for economic uncertainty. It projects its assigned and unassigned reserves at 3.4%, 3.3% and 3.2% over the three years.

cites.quote: The District has fully met the 3% State required reserve for economic uncertainty.
The district’s assigned and unassigned reserve levels are projected at 3.4%, 3.3%, and 3.2%

quotes.quote: To secure a positive certification and uphold a positive fund balance, the District is required to implement $7.0 million in budget balancing adjustments for the 2027-28 fiscal year and an additional $0.5 million for 2028-29, as detailed in the following section.

The Multi-Year Projections in the 2026-27 Budget submission identify the need for up to $7.5 million in budget adjustments, which are either reductions in General Fund expenditures and/or increases in General Fund revenues for years 2027-28 and 2028-29.

measure.text: Measure H of 2024, which replaced Measure E1 in 2025-26.

cites.quote: Berkeley Schools Excellence Program (BSEP) Measure H, passed by the voters in 2024 replacing Measure E1 in FY 2025-26 (Fund 04)

amount.quote: Parcel tax revenues from BSEP, Measure H, are projected to total $46.8 million.

pays.text: 66% for high-quality instruction, 27% for what BUSD calls essentials for excellence, and 7% for effective student support.

cites.quote: Of the BSEP revenue, 66% is designated for High Quality Instruction, 27% is designated for Essentials for Excellence and 7% is designated for Effective Student Support.

cites.quote: The Berkeley Public Schools Educator Recruitment and Retention Act of 2020 (BERRA) Measure E passed by the voters in March 2020.

amount.quote: Parcel tax revenues from BERRA, Measure E, are projected to total $12.6 million.

pays.text: 95% for educator pay, and 5% for programs to recruit, keep and develop educators.

cites.quote: Of the BERRA revenue, 5% is designated for Educator Recruitment, Retention and Development Programs, 95% is designated for Educator Compensation.
